row.evidence: Bitrise's pricing comparison lists "Custom SAML, SCIM for OKTA and Microsoft Entra ID" only in the Enterprise column, and its Entra ID SCIM guide says "SCIM provisioning requires an Enterprise plan."
row.notes: Status unchanged (gated, Enterprise, Contact Sales). Flat build-based pricing: Hobby free, Starter from $89/mo billed annually ($99 monthly), Pro from $200/mo annually ($218 monthly); June recorded the monthly prices. Pro has a SAML SSO add-on (price unlisted); a June 2024 Bitrise changelog post says Entra SCIM is also available to workspaces with SAML via add-on, which conflicts with the pricing page and docs (Enterprise only). SCIM 2.0 endpoint supports Okta and Entra via custom/non-gallery apps (Bitrise is not in the Okta OIN or Entra gallery); verified domain and SAML SSO required. Deprovisioning removes the user from the workspace and frees the seat; account is kept. User API (PAT) can list/add org members and groups but has no member-removal endpoint.

scim.notes: The SCIM base URL is shown per workspace in Settings > Single sign-on > SCIM > Connect with IdP; no URL pattern is published.

auth.token_source: Workspace Settings > Single sign-on > SCIM tab > Connect with IdP (requires a verified domain)
auth.notes: Okta uses HTTP Header authorization mode with the SCIM token; the token can be regenerated, which invalidates the old one.

operations.notes: PUT/PATCH payloads documented in the roles section; PATCH active:false and DELETE both deprovision; re-provisioning the same email is supported.

deprovision.data_retained: Account is not deleted; user is removed from the workspace and all its groups; workflows and secrets are preserved and not reassigned.

custom.how: roles accepts only the built-in values workspace:workspace_viewer, workspace:workspace_contributor, workspace:workspace_manager and rde:rde_admin; custom roles cannot be assigned.

roles.how: SCIM roles attribute with values <family>:<role_name> (workspace viewer/contributor/manager, rde:rde_admin); a present roles array replaces all roles; project-level CI/Release Management roles cannot be set via SCIM; default role Viewer.

limitations.text: SCIM supported only for Okta and Microsoft Entra ID, both as custom/non-gallery apps.
Push Groups is mandatory: workspace membership is managed through groups; without it users are provisioned but not added to any group.
Users on unverified domains cannot be managed via SCIM.
Global Access groups and SAML default groups cannot be deleted via SCIM.
Custom workspace roles and project-level roles cannot be assigned through SCIM.

capabilities.notes: No endpoint to remove a member from the organization is listed in the Swagger spec.

endpoints.purpose: Add a member to the organization by email
Add a group to the organization
Add a member to a group
Replace the groups holding a role on an app

audit_log_api.notes: 'Audit Log Connector' add-on; delivery mechanism not researched.

limitations.text: No documented API endpoint removes a member from an organization/workspace.

okta.notes: Not an OIN app; customers create a custom SAML 2.0 app and enable SCIM provisioning on it.

entra.notes: Not an Entra gallery app; uses Microsoft's non-gallery SCIM configuration.

google.notes: Bitrise publishes a Google SSO guide; SCIM is only supported for Okta and Entra.

onelogin.notes: Bitrise publishes a OneLogin SSO guide; SCIM is only supported for Okta and Entra.

conflicts.text: The pricing page and Entra SCIM guide put SCIM on Enterprise only, while a June 2024 Bitrise changelog post says Entra SCIM is available to Enterprise workspaces 'or those with access to SAML SSO via an add-on'. The pricing page (more specific, current) is used.
The Entra SCIM guide says deprovisioned users' personal access tokens remain active but lose workspace access; the Okta guide says users are logged off and their PATs are disabled.

Whether JIT provisioning on SAML login is supported is not stated in the pages loaded.
SCIM filtering, pagination and rate limits are not documented.
Whether SCIM works on Pro with the SAML add-on (per the 2024 changelog) is unresolved.
